Voters rejected data centers. Will the new Congress regulate artificial intelligence?

November 11, 2026

Listen and subscribe: Apple | Spotify | Wherever You Listen

Sign up to receive our twice-weekly News & Politics newsletter.

The New Yorker staff writer and historian Jill Lepore joins Tyler Foggatt for a conversation about how public feeling around artificial intelligence, and the backlash to the industry, affected the recent midterm elections. Lepore situates the rebuke to the industry in the history of technological advances, futurist visions in science fiction, and the idea of the “artificial state.” They discuss how voters rejected data centers in forty out of forty-one local ballot initiatives, whether the rising tide of fury at Big Tech will prompt the new Congress to pursue regulation of A.I., and what the scandal surrounding Nvidia’s C.E.O., Jensen Huang, could mean for the future of Silicon Valley.

This week’s reading:

“The New Left,” by Jill Lepore
